items.title: SIPRI: With peace elusive, nuclear weapons make a comeback
items.description: Governments are increasingly turning to nuclear deterrence. As the global arms buildup intensifies, so do the risks, the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute warns.

items.title: Ukraine: Russian drone hits nuclear-fuel storage facility
items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called a Russian attack on a nuclear storage facility near Chernobyl "vile." The UN's nuclear watchdog said no increased radiation had been registered at the site.

items.title: North Korea says nuclear program 'absolutely nonnegotiable'
items.description: Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, has reaffirmed the country's nuclear ambitions ahead of a visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping.

sections.title: Beyond Climate & EU — World News Highlights

items.title: Armenia, once Russia's reliable ally, considers an EU future
items.description: Armenians are set to vote on the country's future geopolitical direction on June 7. The election will be a test of public opinion in the long-standing Russia ally, where the population is increasingly eyeing the EU.

items.title: Zelensky's close European allies set out five conditions for peace talks
items.description: The Ukrainian president's meeting with his staunchest European allies came as US President Donald Trump's focus shifts to the war with Iran.

items.title: Sweden mulls prison for young teens as violent crime rises
items.description: In the fight against escalating gang crime, Sweden's parliament will vote on plans to hold 13-year-olds criminally responsible and, in serious cases, imprison them. Other European nations are also lowering age limits.

items.title: Kosovo PM wins snap vote, but with no majority
items.description: Sunday's vote, the country's third in just over a year, was marked by low turnout. The country's prolonged political crisis has further debilitated an already ailing economy.

items.title: Armenia election: Prime Minister Pashinyan declares victory
items.description: The election result, once confirmed, would cement Pashinyan's Westward push away from Russian influence. It is the first vote since a 2023 crushing military defeat by Azerbaijan.
